Careers Aims and Provisions
Careers Aims and Provisions
All students at Cranbrook school undertake a programme of careers education and development. The Careers programme follows the CEC Equalex Framework approach (Introduce & Inspire; Investigate & Explore; Apply & Demonstrate) and seeks to maximise interaction with a range of alumni, employers and employees to enable students to leave with a clear understanding and ability to navigate their career journeys.
Our careers provision is fully evaluated termly using the Careers and Enterprise Company Compass+ tool. This analyses and evaluates our careers programme against the 8 Gatsby benchmarks of good career guidance, which are mandatory markers set out by the government:
Cranbrook takes a whole-school approach to Careers Education, with all subjects highlighting and developing employability skills and career awareness during curriculum delivery. This is augmented by with additional elements including:
A stable careers programme
Learning from career and labour market information
Addressing the needs of each pupil
Linking curriculum learning to careers
Encounters with employers and employees
Experiences of workplaces
Encounters with further and higher education
Personal guidance

Careers Education is delivered across the full school curriculum, in a specifically designated PSHE and tutorial programme and via a range of different opportunities and events that collectively span all year groups. The programme is led by Mrs Corney, our Careers Director and Careers Lead, who should be the first point of contact for any careers-related enquiries from parents, employers, education and training providers on corneye@cranbrook.kent.sch.uk
Students can request a Careers Interview by emailing careers@cranbrook.kent.sch.uk or by asking any of the Careers Team directly. The Careers & Library team are available most break and lunchtimes in the main school library.

A-Level Results 2025
Cranbrook School is delighted and proud to announce the remarkable achievements of its students in this year’s A-Level examinations, achieving an outstanding 38.4% of grades at A*- A, with an impressive 66.4% grades awarded being A* – B.
Our upper sixth students have secured places at prestigious universities across the UK and abroad, including Cambridge, Bath, Durham, Edinburgh, Exeter, UCL, LSE and Imperial. This reflects not only the academic prowess of our students but also the supportive and enriching environment at Cranbrook.
An impressive number of the cohort will be heading off to their choice of university to study courses as diverse as art, economics, engineering and medicine. A reflection of the breadth and diversity on offer at Cranbrook.
As we celebrate these remarkable achievements, we extend our heartfelt congratulations to the entire Class of 2025. Your hard work, resilience and dedication have not only brought you outstanding academic success but have also prepared you for the exciting paths that lie ahead. Whether you’re heading to university, starting a new career or taking time to explore the world, we wish you all the best in your future endeavours. We are immensely proud of all you have accomplished and we look forward to seeing the remarkable contributions you will undoubtedly make in the years to come as Old Cranbrookians. Best of luck to each and every one of you!

Cranbrook School students are once again celebrating outstanding GCSE results. We are extremely proud of their efforts, and these results are a testament to the hard work and dedication of both our students and staff. An impressive 53.4% of grades were achieved at levels 9 to 7, the equivalent of A* – A under the previous grading system, and 95.8% of grades at levels 9 to 4 (A* – C).
David Clark, Head, commented:
“There was a wonderful buzz at Cranbrook School this morning as students returned to collect their GCSE results. It was great to see so many happy students – who had either met or surpassed their academic expectations… and we are immensely proud of their collective achievements. The vast majority are returning to Cranbrook for Sixth Form and I know that they will make a really positive impact as senior students at the School. As always sadly, there will be some students who don’t return for a variety of reasons and we wish them well as they embark on new educational adventures.”

Scholarships
Cranbrook School Scholarships for 2026 Entry
Cranbrook School will be offering the following Scholarships, as agreed and funded by the School’s Trustees.
Students will have the opportunity to register for Scholarship Exams once they are on roll at Cranbrook School.
Students who successfully gain a place at Cranbrook School at 13+ are encouraged to put themselves forward for the Subject Scholarship Programme if they exhibit a real passion and skill in a subject. In addition to recognition, successful students will take part in academic enrichment through the Scholarship Programme. Students are informed of the Application process in the opening weeks of their first term at Cranbrook, with examinations taking place at the latter end of the first half term. Preparation may, of course, take place in advance of joining the School. Recognising the prestige of the Scholarships, feeder Schools are informed of students’ successes.
There are no Scholarships for those applying for Year 7 entry.
Scholarships will be awarded in the following categories:
3 x Entrance Scholarships
Criteria will be based on exceptional performance in the 13+ Entrance Examination, in addition to one Scholarship Paper (as detailed below).
14 x Academic Scholarships
Criteria will be based on high performance in the 13+ Entrance Examination and exceptional performance in one of the following Scholarship Papers: Mathematics, English, Science, French or Spanish, Geography or History and Latin. Furthermore, recognising the importance of practical skills and creativity, teacher assessments will replace traditional exams for subjects such as Physical Education, Drama, Art, Religious Education, Food Preparation and Nutrition, and Computer Science. These assessments allow for a more nuanced evaluation of a candidate’s proficiency and talent in areas that are not easily measured through written tests. Potential scholars are to seek out the specific Head of Department for further guidance.
Scholarship students will receive a prize.
Cranbrook School will be offering two Music Scholarships, as agreed and funded by the School’s Trustees.
2 x Music Scholarships
The Music Scholarships cover the cost of a year’s lessons in the appropriate instrument/voice. Candidates will be expected to have achieved at least the standard of a Grade V and taking or going to take GCSE music.
Successful candidates are required to make a significant contribution to the school’s extra-curricular music programme throughout their time at Cranbrook School.
The School’s decision is final. No appeal is available.
Please contact Dr Darby if you require any further information about the scheme.

School History
Rooted in Tradition, Shaping the Future
Cranbrook School, nestled in the heart of Kent, has a rich history dating back to the 16th century. Founded in 1518 by John Blubery and six other members of Cranbrook Parish, the school was established as a grammar school for boys, reflecting the early Tudor commitment to education. The founders’ vision was to create a place where young people could develop not only in academics but also in character and discipline, in keeping with the values of the era. Over the centuries, Cranbrook School has grown and evolved, yet it remains deeply connected to its founding principles of educational excellence and community service.
The Early Years
The original schoolhouse, a modest building in the centre of Cranbrook, quickly became a beacon for learning. As one of the earliest grammar schools in Kent, Cranbrook School set a standard for rigorous academic preparation, initially focusing on classical studies. Latin and Greek were staples of the curriculum, ensuring that students were well-versed in the classical foundations of learning. By the 17th century, Cranbrook had expanded its curriculum and earned a reputation for developing critical thinkers and leaders, many of whom went on to make their mark in England and beyond.
18th and 19th Century Expansion
As education reform swept through England in the 18th and 19th centuries, Cranbrook School adapted to meet new educational demands. The school expanded both its physical footprint and academic offerings. With the introduction of subjects like mathematics, sciences, and modern languages, Cranbrook evolved into a more diverse academic institution. New facilities were built, including science labs and a library, positioning the school as a forward-thinking institution that blended traditional values with modern educational standards. During this period, Cranbrook also welcomed its first international students, marking the start of a global community that continues to grow today.
20th Century – Coeducation and Growth
The 20th century marked a transformative period for Cranbrook School. In 1972, the school transitioned from a boys-only institution to a coeducational grammar school, reflecting the changing views on gender and education. This pivotal decision allowed Cranbrook to further its mission of educational inclusivity and excellence, opening doors for young women to benefit from its rich academic and pastoral programmes.
As the century progressed, Cranbrook School continued to invest in its facilities, with significant expansions to accommodate a growing student population. The addition of modern sports facilities, enhanced boarding accommodations, and new academic buildings underscored Cranbrook’s commitment to providing a holistic education that supports students’ intellectual, physical, and emotional development.
Cranbrook Today – A Legacy of Excellence
In recent years, Cranbrook School has maintained its prestigious position among Kent grammar schools while embracing 21st-century educational priorities, including sustainability, global citizenship, and community engagement. With a commitment to fostering curiosity, integrity, and kindness, the school prepares students not only for academic success but also to be thoughtful, engaged young people.
As the only school in the UK with a formal sustainability rating, Cranbrook continues to set benchmarks in responsible education, with initiatives across campus that promote environmental stewardship. This commitment is mirrored in the school’s vibrant co-curricular offerings, ranging from sports to music, art, and debating, ensuring every student finds their passion and builds the skills necessary for lifelong learning.

Appeals
Appeal Dates & Information
PLEASE READ THIS CAREFULLY.
If you have not been offered a place at Cranbrook School, the law entitles you to appeal against that decision to an Independent Appeal Panel. This panel is completely independent of the school and the Local Authority. All appeals will be heard online which has the advantage that your appeal can be heard from your home or place of work.
If you wish to appeal, please use this link to complete your appeal online. Please do NOT use ANY other appeal form or send your form to your local authority.
For Sixth Form appeals, please click on this link. Please DO NOT use the normal appeal form for Sixth Form appeals.
It is suggested you should read the explanatory booklet before you complete the appeal form – Booklet Link .
You should include any evidence or supporting material with your appeal form and you MUST give the grounds for your appeal at the time you lodge your appeal form. Your appeal form will not be accepted unless you state the grounds for your appeal. You may appeal for more than one school, but on different forms.
Examples of schoolwork your child may have undertaken will not be accepted. The appeals code is clear that the panel cannot assess a child. The Panel would not be able to make a proper judgement about its quality. They would have nothing to measure it against and would not know the depth of the work submitted. Also, they would not know whether the work had been carried out unaided. The panel will give due weighting to academic letters from professionals such as, headteachers, teachers and tutors, plus CAT or NFER test reports.
Any letters or reports that you wish the panel to see should be uploaded at this time. You are asked to bear in mind that if you later send additional information, the closing date is 12 noon, 5 working days before the STAGE 1 hearing. All appointed panels have agreed NOT to take any late letters or reports after the 5 working day deadline. This will be strictly enforced. For secondary/primary transfer appeals, the hearing will take place at least TWO months after the refusal letter. This gives you plenty of time to get your evidence together if you act early and take account of school holidays.
Please note that the online form will ask you to download two utility bills dated in the last THREE months. If you do not have access to a scanner, please take two photographs with a mobile phone and upload the photographic files.
Full details about the hearing will be sent to you with your invitation to the hearing.
If you wish to contact the clerk – email: clerk@educationappeals.com
Please see the attached download for full details of the appeals timetable.

Drama
The Drama Department is at the heart of creative life at Cranbrook School, based in the vibrant Performing Arts Centre. Central to our drama activities is The Queen’s Hall Theatre, a dedicated space that hosts an array of curricular, co-curricular and external performances throughout the year.
A Stage for Everyone
At Cranbrook, there are countless opportunities for students to take to the stage. Each year, we hold a Whole School Production, alternating between a play and a musical, as well as a Junior Production. These performances are open to all students, encouraging participation and collaboration across year groups. Additionally, GCSE and A Level drama students present their exam pieces to a public audience, offering further opportunities to perform and share their work.
Drama Clubs & Enrichment
For younger students, we run two Junior Drama Clubs:
These clubs provide an excellent opportunity for students to build their confidence, develop acting skills and enjoy the camaraderie of working as a team.
LCM Examinations
Students also have the chance to take London College of Music (LCM) examinations within the Drama Department. Lessons are taught by a visiting LCM specialist on a peripatetic basis, enabling students to hone their performance skills and achieve recognised qualifications.
Behind the Scenes
The Queen’s Hall Theatre is managed by our dedicated Theatre Manager, with invaluable support from the school’s student-led technical team. This team receives professional training in areas such as lighting, sound, and stage management. They play a key role in ensuring the success of internal and external performances, gaining hands-on experience and technical expertise.
Discover More
Drama at Cranbrook School is more than just performance—it’s about fostering creativity, confidence and collaboration. For a closer look at what’s happening at The Queen’s Hall Theatre, visit their website: Queen’s Hall Theatre.

Trip, Tours & Exchanges
At Cranbrook School, we believe that some of the most meaningful learning happens beyond the classroom. Our vibrant programme of trips, tours and exchanges provides students with opportunities to explore new cultures, develop independence and create lasting memories. These experiences are designed to complement the curriculum and foster personal growth, curiosity, and global awareness.
Educational Trips
Educational trips are an integral part of our students’ learning journey. From history excursions to museums and battlefields, to geography fieldwork in unique landscapes, our trips bring subjects to life. These outings allow students to deepen their understanding, apply classroom knowledge in real-world contexts and spark their curiosity.
Sports & Performing Arts Tours
Cranbrook’s sporting and performing arts tours offer students the chance to showcase their talents on a broader stage. Sports teams travel both within the UK and abroad to compete in tournaments, while music and drama groups participate in performances, workshops and festivals. These tours are invaluable in building teamwork, confidence and cultural appreciation.
International Exchanges
Our exchange programmes provide students with immersive experiences in other countries. By living with host families and attending partner schools, students gain a first-hand understanding of different cultures, languages and lifestyles. These exchanges nurture resilience, adaptability and empathy, equipping students with skills for a global future.
Outdoor Adventures
Outdoor education is a cornerstone of Cranbrook’s ethos. Trips such as Duke of Edinburgh expeditions and activity weeks encourage students to challenge themselves, develop teamwork and enjoy the natural environment. Whether navigating a mountain trail or paddling along a river, these adventures build resilience and foster a love of the outdoors.
A World of Opportunity
Cranbrook School is proud to offer students opportunities to explore destinations near and far. Previous trips have included:
Expeditions to Iceland and Costa Rica
Language immersion trips to France and Spain
History tours to the battlefields of Belgium
Geography fieldwork in the Lake District
Music tours to Europe
The Cranbrook Difference
Our trips, tours and exchanges are carefully planned to provide enriching, safe and unforgettable experiences. Whether students are exploring new cultures, testing their limits on an outdoor expedition or gaining new perspectives in their academic subjects, these opportunities form a vital part of their development.
